title: Discovery of Electrophiles and Profiling of Enzyme Cofactors
protocol: Determine probe-reactive proteins using RP-ABPP methodology.
Treat cells with probe and perform lysis.
Conjugate labeled proteins to biotin-azide reporter tag.
Enrich conjugated proteins using streptavidin beads.
Analyze enriched proteins via quantitative mass spectrometry (MS).
Validate identified proteins through recombinant expression protocols.
Treat cells with probe.
Harvest and enrich proteome from cells after treatment.
Design probe including a reactive nucleophile, linker/scaffolds, and an alkyne handle.
Prepare competitor as analog of probe without the alkyne handle.
Grow heavy cells in medium containing 13C- and 15N-enriched amino acid isotopologues.
Grow light cells in medium containing natural-abundance lysine and arginine.
Treat heavy cells with probe in enrichment experiments.
Treat light cells with non-clickable competitor as control in enrichment experiments.
Treat heavy cells the same way as in enrichment experiments for competition experiments.
Treat light cells with probe and an excess amount of competitor (10×) in competition experiments.
Prepare working stock solutions of probe and competitor in H2O with or without 10% DMSO.
Titrate the solutions to pH ∼6.5-7 with concentrated sodium hydroxide using Colorphast pH indicator strips.
Store solutions in aliquots at –80°C.
Grow low-passage human embryonic kidney (HEK293T) and human breast cancer (MDA-MB-231) adherent cell lines in a humidified 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Expand cells in DMEM containing high glucose, L-glutamine, and pyruvate supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin antibiotic/antimycotic.
Plate cells and grow them to near complete confluence at the time of treatment.
Wash cells with ice-cold PBS (pH 7.4).
Replenish cells with serum-free DMEM (∼15% of normal passage volume).
Supplement DMEM with 10 mM Na-HEPES buffer (pH 7.5).
Incubate cells with probe at concentrations of 3 and 1 mM for alkyl and aryl probes, respectively.
Add a 10-fold excess non-clickable analogs as competitors if present, in amounts of 30 and 10 mM for propyl and phenyl hydrazine, respectively.
Premix probe and competitor before administering to cells together when applicable.
Wash cells with ice-cold PBS to remove the probe-containing medium.
Harvest cells by scraping them from the surface.
Collect harvested cells by centrifugation at 1400 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellets in ice-cold PBS and wash again.
Freeze washed cell pellets at -80°C for long-term storage.
Resuspend cell pellets on ice in PBS (100-500 μl).
Lysate cells with a Branson Sonifier probe sonicator using two sets of 6-10 pulses at 15% duty cycle and output setting 3-5.
Adjust resuspension volume and sonication power based on cell pellet yield.
Separate soluble and membrane proteomes by ultracentrifugation for 30-45 min at 100,000 × g, 4°C.
Determine protein concentrations for each fraction using the DC protein assay™ on a microplate reader.
Prepare SILAC sample for MS-based analysis of probe-labeled proteins following in situ labeling protocol steps 1-5.

Passage each cell line a minimum of six doublings in SILAC DMEM containing dFBS supplemented with isotopically enriched L-[13C615N2]lysine hydrochloride and L-[13C615N4]arginine hydrochloride or natural-abundance isotopologues (100 μg/ml each, 550 and 475 μM, respectively).
Treat isotopically light cells with non-clickable analog at the same concentration of probe in “enrichment” experiments.
In competition experiments, treat isotopically light cells with the probe in presence of a 10-fold excess non-clickable analog as competitor.
Perform treatments on isotopically heavy cells with the probe for both types of experiments.
Treatments are conducted in non-SILAC medium.
Mix isotopically heavy and light whole cell lysates in equal proportions.
Follow the proteome preparation procedure described in steps 6-8, starting with lysing the cells.
Dilute the fractionated equimolar mixture of heavy and light soluble proteomes (∼1-1.5 mg) to 1 ml in PBS.
Add 60 µl of a freshly prepared TBTA solution (1.7 mM in 4:1 DMSO:t-BuOH) to each sample (1 ml).
Add 20 µl of a freshly prepared CuSO4 solution (50 mM in H2O) to each sample.
Add 10 µl of biotin-azide solution (10 mM in DMSO) to each sample.
Add 20 µl of freshly prepared TCEP solution (50 mM in PBS or H2O) to each sample.
Vortex the mixture and place on a rotator at ambient temperature for 1 hr.
Quench the reaction by adding prechilled methanol (MeOH; 2 ml).
Quench the reaction by adding chloroform (CHCl3, 0.5 ml) after MeOH addition.
Quench the reaction by adding PBS (1 ml) after CHCl3 addition.
Centrifuge the precipitated proteome 10 min at 5000 × g, 4°C to fractionate the protein interphase from the organic and aqueous solvent layers.
Wash the protein pellet with ice-cold 1:1 (v/v) MeOH:CHCl3 three times, 1 ml each time.
Add ice-cold 4:1 (v/v) MeOH:CHCl3 (2.5 ml).
Sonicate the mixture (5 pulses, 15% duty cycle, output setting 3-5).
Pellet the remaining precipitate by centrifugation at 5000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Redissolve the pellet by mild sonication with 3-5 pulses at a 15% duty cycle and output setting of 3-5 in a freshly prepared solution of 6 M proteomics-grade urea in PBS (500 μl).
Reduce disulfides with TCEP (9 mM) pre-neutralized with potassium carbonate (27 mM) for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Pre-neutralize TCEP with potassium carbonate by adding 600 mM K2CO3 to prepared 200 mM TCEP in a 1:1 volume ratio.
Alkylate reduced thiols with iodoacetamide (45 mM) for 30 minutes at ambient temperature protected from light.
Add 10% SDS stock solution to the mixture to reach a final concentration of 2% SDS to ensure complete denaturation.
Dilute the solution to approximately 0.2% SDS with PBS (∼5 ml).
Incubate the diluted solution on a column containing pre-equilibrated streptavidin agarose resin (50 μl column volume, 100 μl slurry) for ∼1.5-2 hours at ambient temperature on a rotator.
Collect streptavidin beads by centrifugation for 1-2 minutes at 1400 × g.
Wash the collected beads sequentially three times each with 0.2% SDS in PBS (∼10 ml), detergent-free PBS (∼10 ml), and H2O (∼10 ml).
Transfer the resin to a Protein LoBind tube.
Digest bound proteins on-bead overnight at 37°C in ∼200 μl total volume containing sequencing-grade porcine trypsin (2 μg) in the presence of 2 M urea in PBS and 1 mM CaCl2.
Transfer the proteolyzed supernatant to a fresh Protein LoBind tube.
Acidify the supernatant with formic acid (5%) to inactivate trypsin.
Store the treated supernatant at −80°C if needed.
Desalt the acidified peptide mixture using C18 Stage Tips.
Concentrate desalted samples under reduced pressure in an evacuated centrifuge (SpeedVac).
Redissolve concentrated samples in 10 μl of diluent (98% H2O, 2% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) for nanoLC-MS/MS analysis.

Inject a 3- to 5-μl aliquot of the solution via a nano-LC system onto a 75-μm-inner-diameter fused-silica capillary column hand-packed with C18 resin and with a laser-pulled tip in solvent A (0.1% formic acid in H2O).
Develop the column with a 60-min gradient of 5%-100% solvent B (20% H2O, 80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid).
Ionize peptides in positive-ion mode with a flow rate of 300 nl/min and an applied voltage of 2.3 kV.
Collect spectra in data-dependent mode.
Include a single high-resolution (30,000) full MS spectrum of parent ions (MS1 scan from 400 to 1800 m/z) collected in the Orbitrap Fusion.
Induce fragmentation with CID for 30 most abundant parent ions from the MS1 scan.
Exclude parent ions with unassigned +1 charge stated by the instrument for fragmentation.
Extract MS2 spectra for all fragmented parent ions (.ms2 file) from .raw files generated by the instrument using RAW Xtract or RawConverter with monoisotopic selection.
Search each .ms2 file using ProLuCID algorithm against a reverse-concatenated, nonredundant database of the human proteome within IP2 software.
Filter search results using DTASelect 2.0 within IP2 software.
Apply static modification for carboxyamidomethylation (+57.02146 Da) to cysteine residues during search.
Search methionine residues with up to one differential modification for oxidation (+15.9949 Da).
Require peptides to have at least one tryptic terminus.
Allow an unlimited number of missed cleavages in the database search.
Specify the mass shift of heavy residues as static modifications on lysine (+8.0142 Da).
Specify the mass shift of heavy residues as static modifications on arginine (+10.0082 Da).
Set the parent ion mass tolerance for a minimum envelope of three isotopic peaks to 50 ppm.
Set the minimum peptide length to six residues.
Require the false positive rate to be 1%.
Require the detection of at least two peptides of a protein.
Extract heavy and light parent ion chromatograms associated with successfully identified peptides using in-house software.
Compare heavy and light parent ion chromatograms associated with successfully identified peptides.
Ensure that at least one ion of a coeluting heavy-light pair is accurately identified from a fragmentation event within the retention time window (±10 min).
Quantify the correct pair of peaks by extracting chromatograms within a 10-ppm error tolerance of the predicted m/z.
Require single-to-noise ratios >2.5 for quantification.
Ensure “co-elution correlation scores” and “envelope correlation scores” R2 values ≥0.8 for quantification.
Grow cells to ∼40% confluence under standard growth conditions, passaging in the appropriate medium.
Add 4 µg of expression vector and polyethyleneimine (PEI) “MAX” (MW 40,000) as a transfection reagent under standard transfection conditions with a vector/PEI ratio of 3:1 (w/w).
Incubate cells for ∼48 hr before performing in situ labeling and proteome preparation.
Dilute soluble proteomes from treated cells to 1 mg/ml, 50 μl.
Add 6 μl of the "click" reagent mixture to each sample.
Mix by vortexing immediately after addition.
Allow the reaction to proceed at ambient temperature for 1 hour while rotating.
Quench the reactions with 4× SDS loading buffer (17 µl).
Resolve proteins by SDS-PAGE using a 10% acrylamide gel.
Load approximately 25 μg total protein per gel lane.
Visualize proteins by in-gel fluorescence scanning on a flatbed fluorescence scanner.
Transfer the same gel to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Perform western blotting as described in Matthews et al., 2017.
Use isoTOP-ABPP experiments to find the peptide labeled.
Employ a hybrid sequencing approach to identify the specific amino acid residue labeled.
Apply a site-specific profiling method called isoTOP ABPP to identify the peptide labeled.
Leverage isotopically differentiated, protease-cleavable biotin-TEV tags after probe treatment of non-SILAC cells.
Enrich labeled proteomes on streptavidin beads following conjugation to heavy and light tags.
Perform on-bead digestion.
Discard unlabeled peptides.
Release labeled peptides from beads through cleavage of the tag using TEV protease.
Plot coeluting pairs of heavy and light tags in dark and light green, respectively.
Identify peptide harboring the labeled residue by its mass shift.
Sequence MS2 spectral assignments to determine residue(s) containing modification.
Calculate mass of bound electrophile within 1 ppm error.
Mutate specific residue for validation and confirmation.
Treat wild-type or transfected cells with probe after in situ labeling as described in Basic Protocol 1, steps 4-8.
Dilute soluble proteomes (2 mg total protein) to 1 ml in PBS.
Conjugate half of the proteome (0.5 ml) to the light TEV tag and the other half to the heavy TEV tag.
Scale click reactions to maintain final concentrations of 0.1 mM TBTA, 1 mM CUSO4, 100 μM of 5 mM light or heavy biotin-TEV-azide in DMSO, and 1 mM TCEP.
Vortex the mixture and place on a rotator at ambient temperature for 1 h.
Centrifuge samples 5 min at 16,000 × g, 4°C.
Add ice-cold methanol (0.5 ml) to the centrifuged samples.
Mildly sonicate resulting pellets (3-5 pulses, 15% duty cycle, output setting 3-5).
Combine the light- and heavy-labeled proteomes.
Centrifuge the combined proteomes once more.
Solubilize the proteomes with 1.2% SDS in PBS using sonication.
Store the solubilized samples at –80°C overnight if desired.
Dilute the samples to approximately 0.2% SDS in PBS (approximately 5 ml).
Incubate diluted samples with pre-equilibrated streptavidin agarose resin for 2-3 hours at ambient temperature while rotating.
Wash the resin as described in Basic Protocol 1, step 9(m).
Transfer the washed resin to fresh microcentrifuge tubes.
Resuspend the resin in 6 M urea in PBS (500 μl).
Reduce cysteines with TCEP according to Basic Protocol 1, step 9(i).
Alkylate cysteines with iodoacetamide as described in Basic Protocol 1, step 9(j).
Wash the resin once with PBS to remove reagents.
Digest bound proteins with trypsin (2 μg) for 8-12 hours at 37°C in the presence of 2 M urea and 2 mM CaCl2 in PBS (200 μl).
Remove unmodified peptides, urea, and trypsin by sequential washes with PBS five times (0.5 ml each) and H2O five times (0.5 ml each).
Transfer the resin to fresh tubes.
Equilibrate the resin with TEV buffer (50 mM Tris, pH 8).
Release remaining immobilized peptides with approximately 1-2 μM TEV protease in 200 μl of TEV buffer at 30°C for 3-5 hours while shaking gently.
Collect and recover heavy- and light-labeled peptides from the resin by elution with H2O (two washes, 50 μl each).
Desalt the samples using C18 stage tips.
Store desalted samples at –80°C.
Analyze proteomics data as described in Basic Protocol 1, step 10.
Search MS1 spectra for paired coeluting peaks differing by 6.0138 Da (±5 ppm).
Consider +2 and +3 charge state differences when searching for isotopic partners.
Require the monoisotopic peak intensity to be ≥5% of the base peak in each spectrum.
Ensure at least three peaks are present in each isotope profile.
Set a Euclidean distance threshold ≤0.2 between two isotope profiles.
Group pairs with identical m/z values (±5 ppm) and retention times to eliminate duplicates.
Analyze pairs of parent ions from transfected versus mock-transfected cells.
Search through three biological replicates.
Perform MS1 searches to find coeluting pairs with specified mass differences.
Assign MS2 spectra by de novo sequencing to determine the residue labeled.
Modify instrument method for high-resolution data collection in Orbitrap Fusion instrument (resolutions for MS1 and MS2 set at 30,000 and 7500, respectively).
Select only the five most abundant parent ions for fragmentation per cycle in Orbitrap Fusion instrument.
Extend number of MS2 spectra collected per cycle to ten if generated on Orbitrap instrument.
Search MS2 spectra for diagnostic ions of peptide.
Find highly abundant fragments representing diagnostic markers for unmodified portion and modified portion with isotopic tags.
Compare spectra for heavy and light peptides observing appropriate ion shift (6.0138 Da).
Use RawConverter to extract accurate monoisotopic m/z values for each MS2 spectra.
Generate mutants with primers containing the desired mutations and their respective complements.
Transfect cells as described above in validation via recombinant expression.
Label and prepare proteomes as described above in in situ labeling and proteome preparation sections.
Conjugate to fluorophore.
Visualize via in-gel fluorescence.
Perform western blotting as described above in Basic Protocol 1.
Confirm the site if mutation of the site results in visualization of a loss of probe labeling while expression of both the wild-type and mutant proteins remains present (confirmed via western blot).
Propose a structure match using mass information about the probe-captured PTM from de novo sequencing and chemical intuition about the residue and probe chemical reactivity.
Confirm the proposed structure by coeluting peptides with synthetic standards.
Quantify the fraction of protein bearing the modification inside the cell using peptide coelution protocol.
Validate electrophilic site and structure utilizing coelution of isotopically differentiated samples.
Use light synthesized peptide with proposed probe-captured electrophile PTM for validation.
Synthesize SCRN3 probe–captured glyoxylyl tryptic peptide using solid-phase peptide synthesis as previously described.
Dilute stocks of the heavy and light biotin-azide tags (0.25 μmol each) to 250 μM with 1 ml 50 mM Tris•Cl, pH 8, supplemented with 1 mM DTT in the presence of 0.4 μM TEV protease.
Incubate the reaction overnight at 30°C.
Concentrate the reaction to ∼200 µl.
Precipitate the protease with an equal volume of acetonitrile and pellet.
Purify the supernatants containing the products by reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography.
Use a Phenomenex Jupiter 5 μm C18 300 Å column with a flow rate of 1 ml/min.
Apply a gradient of 0%-70% 90:10 (v/v) acetonitrile/H2O in H2O, 0.05% (v/v) TFA over 35 min.
Conjugate hydrazone alkyne peptide to cleaved heavy and light tags via Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition.
Add TBTA at a concentration of 0.1 mM, CuCl2 at 1 mM, and TCEP at 1 mM.
Mix these with a 0.5-ml mixture of the hydrazone alkyne peptide (∼0.3 mM, ∼0.15 μmol).
Combine this with either form of cleaved tag (∼60 μM, ∼0.03 μmol of each) in sodium phosphate buffer (60 mM, pH 7).
Incubate reactions at ambient temperature for ∼2 hr.
Purify by RP-HPLC using a Phenomenex Jupiter 5μm C18 300 Å (150 × 4.6 mm) column.
Neutralize the product with sodium phosphate buffer (25 mM, pH 7).
Lyophilize the neutralized product.
Freeze in aliquots (5-50 pmol each) at –80°C.
Coelute tagged peptide pairs of protein labeled with probe as described in Basic Protocol 2, step 1.
Grow cells in standard SILAC medium for labeling.
Isolate tagged peptides from the sample.
Analyze the sample in the absence and presence of 0.5 pmol of natural-abundance synthetic standards modified with probe and conjugated with tags.
Dilute standard in water.
Verify concentration spectrophotometrically.
Add 0.5 pmol to the digested sample just before loading the column for analysis.
Transfect cells grown in heavy SILAC medium using a plasmid containing genes for the protein and FLAG.
Lysate cells in PBS (pH 7.4) and fractionate by ultracentrifugation at 100,000 × g for 30-40 min at 4°C.
Dilute the sample to 1 ml with 50 mM Na-HEPES buffer (pH 7.5), supplemented with 500 mM NaCl and 1% Triton X-100.
Pellet unsolubilized protein by centrifugation, denature with a small volume of 10% SDS for 1 hr at 37°C, recombine with diluted reaction ensuring final concentration of SDS does not exceed ∼0.2%.
Incubate the resolubilized sample with anti-FLAG resin overnight at 4°C by rotation.
Wash resin by resuspension and centrifugation in buffer supplemented with only 500 mM NaCl (5 × 1 ml) followed by only 100 mM NaCl (2 × 1 ml).
Elute the bound protein by incubating beads in PBS containing 8 M urea twice, 50 µl each time for ∼1 hr at 37°C.
Reduce cysteines with 10 mM TCEP (pre-neutralized with 30 mM potassium carbonate) for 30 min at 37°C and alkylate with 20 mM iodoacetamide under the same conditions but protected from light.
Dilute samples to 2 M urea in PBS, add 2 μg trypsin supplemented with 1 mM CaCl2, incubate overnight at 37°C for tryptic digestion.
Inactivate trypsin with 5% formic acid.
Dope the digested protein sample with the modified standard.
Add an internal peptide representing the total protein (5-50 pmol).
Adjust absolute amounts of standards to achieve comparable peak intensities for quantitation.
